text.p: The Turkish central bank drained 75 trillion lira through interbank and open market deals on Thursday and sold dollars for lira to restrain the U.S. currency's rise, bankers said.

The bank drained 17.9 trillion lira overnight at 57 percent on the interbank and 57.1 trillion lira via three-month reverse repurchase agreements at an average rate of 78.40 percent on the open market.
On Tuesday, it had withdrawn 38.2 trillion lira of surplus cash overnight at the same rate in a shortened trading session before the New Year holiday.
The average overnight rate firmed to 60.21 percent from Tuesday's 57.62 because overnight money mostly traded at around 65 percent during the day.
The lira weakened sharply against the dollar at midday due to some 94 trillion lira of idle cash fuelling dollar demand after the central bank's reverse repurchase auction.
The lira sank to 108,560 to the dollar from an opening of 108,200 and compared to Tuesday's 108,290 close.
Bankers said the central bank sold dollars to a few banks in early afternoon and intervened again more effectively in late trade, causing the lira to firm to 108,220 at close.
"The central bank sold dollars for lira to a few banks in early afternoon just to check the rates. It intervened more heavily towards the close," a private banker said.
T-bill and bond yields were mixed after rates plunged by 10 to 13 points in the last two days of 1996 on news of a rise in witholding tax on government securities to be issued in 1997.

The average yield on the most heavily traded October 30, 1997 was 100.86 percent, down from 102.86 on Tuesday. The second most active June 4,1997 paper yielded 96.73 percent, up from an average of 95.6 percent on Tuesday.
